newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat condition improves slightly.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat condition improves slightly.

text.p: Oklahoma's wheat condition improved slightly in the week ended Sunday as thunderstorms brought needed moisture to some areas, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.
Wheat was rated 13 percent excellent, 66 percent good, 19 percent fair and two percent poor, as of Sunday. A week earlier the comparative totals were nine, 70, 19 and two.
"Insect pressures continue to increase across the state. Soil-borne mosiac virus, barley yellow dwarf and rust are being reported in several fields," the report said.
Dry conditions continued in many western areas.
Wheat jointing was reported at 68 percent, ahead of 19 percent last year and a five-year average of 54 percent.
Livestock condition remained mostly good across the state.
Topsoil moisture was rated six percent surplus, 61 percent adequate, 27 percent short and six percent very short.
Seedbed preparation for sorghum was 41 percent complete, ahead of 13 percent last year and also ahead of thefive-year average of 23 percent.
